requirement_text:
Functional Requirement

1.1 Goals and objectives
The central trading system (CTS) is to complete the trading of stock. It analyses the instructions that enter the central trading system and divides them into several kinds of instructions. System will make a match between them under specifically prescripts. Also central trading system provides some interfaces to send messages to other modules.
1.2 System Context
The CTS is just a subsystem of the whole stock trading system (STS) system. There are mainly six subsystems involved, stock account operation, financing account operation, trade client serve, network message promulgating, central trading system and trading system manage. Communications exist among these subsystems which complicates the relationships between subsystems. The CTS receive instructions from trade client serve. Then the CTS produce new messages which to be sent to network message promulgating after deal with the instructions from trade client serve. Also the system manager is authorization to access the information in CTS.
1.3 Potential Users’ Specification
There are mainly two kinds of users. The CTS provides the terminal users easy Operations that are confined to a series of mouse clicks and keyboard, which compared to other systems are really much simplified. However, for another user, things are different .the maintainers of this CTS must be familiar with java programming and the socket. When the system crashes down, they can find the cause and fix it. When new requirements should be supported, they can modify the program to make it fit. As the instruction is frequently operated in CTS such as fetch, deal with, repeal and so on, the CTS is heavily transferred. The program must take this into consideration. The maintainers of CTS should have good strategies to overcome crash of the system when overhead exceeds the capacity of it.

Use case Scenarios

Use-case: Buy stock
Primary actor:	Transaction User Interface
Goal in context: To fulfill the buy transaction
Preconditions:	Customer has successfully logged into UI and submit the buy information
Trigger	The ‘buy’ button on UI been clicked
Scenario:
1.   transaction user interface: give the buy instruction
2.   central trading system: save the buy instruction
3.   central  trading  system:  match  the  instructions  with  the same stock id
4.   central trading system: make a trade by matching
5.   central trading system: modify the information of matched instructions
Exception:
1.    all the operations have been suspended
2.    some trade exceptions come up
3.    no matched stock with the buy instruction
Channel to actor: Via transaction user interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues: 
1.    Should the trade information  return to Transaction  User
Interface immediately when the deal is done?
2.    Should  the  failure  of  trade  return  to  Transaction  User
Interface the next day?
3.    If exception happens, is exception log needed?
4.    security issue

Use-case: Sell stock
Primary actor: Transaction User Interface
Goal in context: To fulfill the sell transaction
Preconditions: Customer has successfully logged into UI and submit the sell information
Trigger: The ‘sell’ button on UI been clicked
Scenario:
1.   transaction user interface: give the sell instruction
2.   central trading system: save the sell instruction
3.   central  trading  system:  match  the  instructions  with  the same stock id
4.   central trading system: make a trade by matching
5.   central trading system: modify the information of matched instructions
Exception:
1.   all the operations have been suspended
2.   some deal exceptions come up
3.   no matched stock with the buy instruction
Channel to actor: Via transaction user interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues:
1.   Should  the trade information  return  to Transaction  User
Interface immediately when the deal is done?
2.   Should  the  failure  of  trade  return  to  Transaction  User
Interface the next day?
3.   If exception happens, is exception log needed?
4.   security issue

Use-case: Cancel trading instruction
Primary actor:	Transaction User Interface
Goal in context: To fulfill the cancel transaction
Preconditions: Customer  has  successfully  logged  into  UI  and  submit  the cancel information
Trigger: The ‘cancel’ button on UI been clicked
Scenario:
1.   transaction user interface: give the cancel instruction
2.   central trading system: save the cancel instruction
3.   central trading system: cancel the correlative instruction
Exception:
1.   all the operations have been suspended
2.   the instruction concerned has been implemented
3.   no matched instruction to be cancelled
Channel to actor: Via transaction user interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues:
1.    Is it necessary to return the status of cancel transaction?
2.    If exception happens, is exception log needed?
3.    security issue


Use-case: Save trade information
Primary actor: Security Account Management
Goal in context: To save all successful trade information
Preconditions:	The  correlative   trade  transactions   have  been   successfully conducted
Trigger: Any trade transaction been conducted
Scenario:
1.   central  trading  system:   give  out  the  successful   trade information
2.   security account management: save the trade information
Exception:
1.   all the operations have been suspended
2.    no matched stock with the buy instruction
Channel to actor: Via central trading system interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues:
1.    If exception happens, is exception log needed?
2.   Will  we  develop  a  media  (ie.  Web  page)  where  any customer can look up the latest trade records which have been saved?
3.    security issue


Use-case: Query trade information
Primary actor:	Trading Information Release
Goal in context: To   query   the   trading   information   which   needed   to   be statistically analyzed and released on a web site
Preconditions: Central Trading System deal transactions well
Trigger: Trading Information Release System send a query
Scenario:
1.   trading information release system: send a query
2.   central trading system: implement the query
3.   central trading system: structuralize the queried data
4.   central trading system: send the data to release
Exception:
1.   all the operations have been suspended
2.   the query is invalid
3.    no matched data
Channel to actor: Via central trading system interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues	
1.    If exception happens, is exception log needed?
2.    How frequent the release system is to send a query?
3.    Do we need a warning if any query failed?
4.    security issue

plan.objective: Model the central trading system (CTS) activity flow for receiving, analyzing, classifying, matching, trading, updating, saving trade information, querying trade information, and handling specified exceptions for buy, sell, cancel, and query use cases.

nodes.label: Receive instructions from trade client serve
Match buy instructions with same stock id
Make trade by matching for buy
Modify matched instruction information for buy
Match sell instructions with same stock id
Make trade by matching for sell
Modify matched instruction information for sell

exceptions.trigger: No matched stock or instruction/data exists
No matched instruction to be cancelled

decision_strategy: Classify incoming instructions into buy, sell, cancel, or query branches.
For buy and sell flows, proceed only if matching instructions with the same stock id are found.
If no matching stock is found, route to the no-match exception handler.
If operations are suspended, route to the suspended-operations handler.
If a cancel target cannot be found or is already implemented, route to the corresponding cancel exception handler.
If a query is invalid or yields no data, route to the query exception handlers.
concurrency_strategy: No explicit parallel activities are specified in the requirements.
exception_strategy: Suspend-operations exceptions terminate the current use-case handling path.
Trade-related exceptions are handled explicitly and then terminate the current path.
No-match conditions are handled explicitly and then terminate the current path without trade completion.
Cancel/query-specific exception conditions are handled explicitly and then terminate the current path.
termination_strategy: The activity ends after successful buy trade completion and trade information save.
The activity ends after successful sell trade completion and trade information save.
The activity ends after successful cancel instruction processing.
The activity ends after successful query implementation and data release.
The activity ends after any handled exception path.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers the main buy/sell/cancel/query flows, but it still has important semantic gaps and one clear behavioral mismodeling relative to the stated requirements. Some non-core operational requirements remain unrepresented, and the sell-use-case exception text is inconsistent with the requirement language.

defects.description: The diagram does not represent the required CTS capability to provide interfaces for sending messages to other modules.
defects.evidence: R5 requires the central trading system to provide interfaces to send messages to other modules, but the activity flow only models trading and query steps and does not include any message-sending interface behavior.
defects.suggested_action: Add a CTS action or interface-related activity that represents sending messages to other modules, or connect the existing flow to such behavior if it is intended to occur after processing.

defects.description: The diagram omits the required post-processing message production and dispatch to the network message promulgating subsystem.
defects.evidence: R7 requires CTS to produce new messages after dealing with instructions from the trade client serve subsystem, and R8 requires those messages to be sent to the network message promulgating subsystem. The diagram ends the main flow after trade information handling and does not model message production or delivery to the network subsystem.
defects.suggested_action: Add activities after instruction processing that produce the required messages and send them to the network message promulgating subsystem.

defects.description: The diagram does not represent the system manager’s authorized access to information in CTS.
defects.evidence: R9 states that the system manager is authorized to access information in CTS, but no activity or access path for the system manager appears in the diagram.
defects.suggested_action: Add a management-access activity or a separate branch showing authorized access to CTS information by the system manager.

defects.description: The diagram does not capture the UI usability/access style requirement for terminal users using mouse clicks and keyboard inputs.
defects.evidence: R10 specifies that the transaction UI provides easy operations via mouse clicks and keyboard inputs, but the diagram only models abstract instruction transfer and does not represent this interaction constraint.
defects.suggested_action: Represent the UI interaction behavior if the diagram is intended to cover UI operation semantics; otherwise model it in a different artifact.

defects.description: The maintainers’ capability and crash/maintenance requirements are not represented in the activity flow.
defects.evidence: R11 through R15 describe maintainer skills, crash recovery, adaptation to new requirements, heavy-transfer consideration, and crash-overhead strategies. The activity diagram models runtime trading flow only and contains no maintainer or operational-resilience behavior.
defects.suggested_action: If these requirements are in scope for the diagram, add maintenance/resilience activities; otherwise keep them out of the activity diagram and trace them in a different model.

defects.description: The sell-stock no-match exception is modeled using the buy-stock wording rather than the sell-stock condition, which conflicts with the requirement text.
defects.evidence: R31 states that the sell-stock use case shall handle the case where no matched stock exists for the sell instruction, but the requirement text itself is incorrectly phrased as 'no matched stock with the buy instruction'. The diagram labels the handler generically, but its traceability to R31 is semantically ambiguous because the modeled exception condition is not explicitly sell-specific.
defects.suggested_action: Rename or annotate the exception handling path so it explicitly refers to the sell instruction no-match case, matching the intended sell-use-case behavior.

strengths: Main buy, sell, cancel, and query sequences are present in the correct general order.
Core trade processing steps are modeled: receive/analyze/divide, then use-case-specific save/match/trade/update actions.
Exception branches are included for suspension, no-match conditions, invalid query, and implemented-instruction cancellation.
The diagram includes a final termination point and connects all main successful flows to completion.
unsupported_behaviors: The sell no-match exception is not explicitly aligned to the sell instruction wording in the requirement set (R31).

changes: Added a CTS action node for prescript-based instruction matching to explicitly represent R4.
Rerouted the flow from instruction division to the new matching action, then into the existing instruction-type decision, preserving existing use-case branches and requirement traces.
repair_history.rationale: The only semantic defect was the missing explicit representation of R4. A new action node was inserted between instruction division and use-case routing so the diagram now shows the CTS matching instructions under specific prescripts without altering the existing buy/sell/cancel/query and exception behavior. Exactly one initial node and at least one final node are preserved, and existing correct nodes/edges remain intact apart from the minimal reroute needed to satisfy R4 and compilation validity.

changes: Connected previously unreachable exception-handling nodes into the main workflow by adding explicit control-flow branches from the existing decision nodes.
Preserved all existing nodes, edges, labels, requirement IDs, and the single initial/final structure; only routing of exception branches was adjusted to eliminate unreachable nodes.
Added explicit guards on all decision outgoing branches already present to maintain valid activity semantics and PlantUML compilability.
repair_history.rationale: The only structural defect reported was unreachable nodes. To fix this with minimal behavioral change, the existing exception-handling actions were integrated as branches from the already existing decision nodes rather than redesigning the flow. This preserves all correct requirement traces and keeps the diagram focused on the supplied buy/sell/cancel/query workflows while ensuring every node is reachable and the activity model remains valid.
